label: no
controls_available: Difficulty 5 uses an 18-by-9 map (162 one-household parcels), 24 boundary-warp steps, four reciprocal exchanges of three parcels per side, a 32-parcel change budget, exact population 18 per canton, and a 5 Gilt / 2 Tide / 2 Plum holding split.

The full surface has nine canton-seal buttons to select the active canton, followed by a left-button brush drag through adjacent visible parcel polygons; a passing run also needs one stroke through at least 5 joined parcels that repaints at least 3 parcels.

UNDO reverts the last assignment event. CERTIFY CHARTER submits the current assignment and is administrative; keyboard is declared in the environment action schema but the charter mechanic installs no keyboard task handler.
autonomous_processes: None after setup/render or between agent events: parcel ownership, history, budget, event transcript, and displayed assignment statistics change only in response to pointer/button handlers.
The 100 ms fill transition is action-triggered CSS presentation only; it does not change task state, hit testing, grading, or the availability/effectiveness of an outcome-affecting action.
grouped_control_modes: D_brush: every full-mode map-brush drag after canton-seal selection, across seeds, rounds, and attempts.
D_undo: every UNDO button action that reverts the most recent assignment event. Certification is administrative and is not an outcome-affecting control mode.

clause_i.reason: For the grouped brush mode, the useful repair depends on the seed-specific visible parcel geometry, current assignment, and guild placement. The generator constructs randomized initial/target partitions, while q(I_t) cannot condition on the current screenshot, so one action-clock-only policy cannot be optimal for every active history.

clause_ii.reason: A single current screenshot is a sufficient bounded window for the static control problem: it shows the parcel polygons, assignment fills, guild house marks, adjacency geometry, and canton seals. With observation_window_ms 0 and one frame, a visual policy can choose a repair from the current state without temporal evidence; this does not supply a real-time process.

clause_iii.reason: No legitimate D has the required autonomous non-clock task-state evolution. The complete charter mechanic has no timer, interval, animation-frame, or physics update that mutates the task between actions, so H_t^tau does not change in the required way for any Delta > 0 and no action's Q value or advantage strictly degrades. The fixed fill transition is only action-triggered presentation.

common_visible_process: There is no common visible autonomous process. After any brush or undo, the map remains at the resulting assignment until another agent event; live task-clock passage or the generic clock infrastructure does not create charter state changes. Consequently the same phenomenon cannot witness clauses (i), (ii), and (iii).

pre_run.reason: No autonomous outcome phase exists: every parcel-assignment change is agent-supplied, and certification is administrative. The configuration already fails the mathematical definition at clause (iii), so the pre-run override is not needed.

source_evidence.claim: The frozen definition requires one common visibly evidenced autonomous process that strictly degrades an action opportunity; static tasks and unrelated or fixed animations fail.
The assigned difficulty-5 profile has 18 columns, 9 rows, 24 displaced parcels, 32 changes, exact population tolerance 0, full interaction, and observation_window_ms 0 with one frame.
Generation uses a seed-derived static construction, creates polygons and assignments once, exposes only the initial assignment publicly, and returns no time-driven state process.

The visible mechanic mutates assignment state only from brush/pointer, seal-button, undo, and submission handlers; its complete file contains no timer, interval, requestAnimationFrame, physics, or autonomous update loop.
The only map transition is a 0.1-second fill/fill-opacity CSS transition after an input-driven repaint, with no task-state or opportunity effect.

The authoritative grader replays the submitted visible assignment/undo transcript and checks geometry, budget, populations, connectivity, holdings, and the full-mode brush requirement; it has no time-dependent outcome rule.
The intended screenshot-only information is visible parcels, guilds, adjacency, and current assignment; the private reference partition is not delivered to the browser.

The scripted solver reads the private target assignment and emits brush/assignment actions, which is implementation evidence rather than policy-visible information; those actions are all agent-triggered.
The environment declares a 240-second play allowance, a zero-length observation window, one frame, and synchronous execution; the allowance is a deadline, not a charter state evolution.

uncertainties: The checked seed fixture retains an older medium/difficulty-3 task record, while the assigned difficulty-5/full profile is explicitly defined in controls.json; the no-autonomous-process finding is unchanged by that fixture mismatch.
